gen-gf-carme-fs-literata: Literata is a serif whose thin and thick strokes sit close together, with curves left wide open, while Carme above it has no hairlines at all. The mix of the two is the real strength.
gen-gf-cause-fs-amulya: Amulya keeps its curves generously open and modern. Cause is the loose, hand-drawn voice with an e flung wide, while the plain sans handles the steady work, comfortable in small doses.
gen-gf-cause-fs-bespoke-sans: Friendly and inviting, Cause leads with a wide-open e and a hand-drawn wobble. Bespoke Sans follows with sharper, refined curves, so the page feels loose on top and tidy beneath.
gen-gf-cause-fs-plein: Plein reads reliable and clean, with a clear channel leading into every round letter, so each line goes down without any fuss. Over a longer passage it would stay plainly easy going.
gen-gf-cause-montserrat: A hand-drawn feel with an e opened wide is what defines Cause, and Montserrat sits beneath it with geometric, oversized counters. A longer passage would feel spacious and approachable.
gen-gf-changa-fs-erode: Dignified and editorial in feel, Erode is the body here. Changa's tall, straight-faced sans heading gives it a crisp lead-in, while the serif below swells gently with its stroke weight.
gen-gf-charm-fs-literata: Charm huddles its hand-drawn letters close, every stroke carrying the same visual weight. Literata, a serif with a slight pinch where curves meet stems, would take a longer passage gracefully despite the note against long paragraphs.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-cardo: Cherry Swash opens its c like a horseshoe, with diagonals as heavy as the verticals. Cardo answers with a classic serif's softly varied strokes, its diagonals slightly thinner, as if gently pressed.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-graduate: A c opened wide like a horseshoe, plus diagonals as heavy as the verticals, make Cherry Swash unmistakable. Graduate sits next to it as a classic serif, dignified and bookish, with generous space between letters.
gen-gf-chilanka-clash-grotesk: Chilanka's strokes never vary in thickness, and its counters stay open to the outside. Clash Grotesk, a sans with no thick-and-thin modulation either, is made for short stretches of reading, so give its size a little extra room.
